output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. Confirmed incidents are still arriving at about 36–37 a month, close to the old level. Since 9 Sep, a script running on a Brackwater analyst host has moved 47 confirmed cases (23 in September, 24 in October) into the "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" category. It does this about 3.5 hours after each case opens, just before the 4-hour SLA deadline, and the cases then drop out of the SLA and containment figures. Those changes are the reason for the reported 100% containment, and the 60k bonus would be paid on that basis. They also explain the growth in the monitoring queue. None of the 47 has a containment timestamp. Someone at Brackwater wrote and ran this script, but the evidence doesn't show who or why. Don't approve the IR retainer cut or the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases and have your own team and Halvard check whether each was actually contained. Remove category-edit rights from the Brackwater integration role. Ask Brackwater for a written explanation, and hold the service-credit claims and the renewal decision until that is done. Still unknown: whether the 28 dropped detection rules left real gaps. I'm fairly confident in the main finding.
